sanskrit: tāṃ kathāṃ kauśiko rāme nivedya madhurākṣaram punar evāparaṃ vākyaṃ kākutstham idam abravīt
english: Having narrated that tale to Rāma in honeyed syllables, Kauśika then spoke again to the descendant of Kakutstha with these further words.

sanskrit: ayodhyādhipatiḥ śūraḥ pūrvam āsīn narādhipaḥ sagaro nāma dharmātmā prajākāmaḥ sa cāprajaḥ
english: There was formerly a heroic king, lord of Ayodhyā, a ruler of men named Sagara, righteous in soul, longing for offspring, yet he was without children.

sanskrit: vaidarbhaduhitā rāma keśinī nāma nāmataḥ jyeṣṭhā sagarapatnī sā dharmiṣṭhā satyavādinī
english: O Rāma, the elder wife of Sagara was the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, named Keśinī, most devoted to dharma and truthful in speech.

sanskrit: ariṣṭanemiduhitā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi dvitīyā sagarasyāsīt patnī sumatisaṃjñitā
english: The second wife of Sagara was the daughter of Ariṣṭanemi, matchless in beauty on earth, known by the name Sumatī.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ saha tadā rājā patnībhyāṃ taptavāṃs tapaḥ himavantaṃ samāsādya bhṛguprasravaṇe girau
english: Together with both those wives the king then performed ascetic practice, resorting to the Himavān mountain, at the peak called Bhṛguprasravaṇa.

sanskrit: atha varṣa śate pūrṇe tapasārādhito muniḥ sagarāya varaṃ prādād bhṛguḥ satyavatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, when a full hundred years had passed, the sage Bhṛgu, best among those steadfast in truth, gratified by the austerity, bestowed a boon upon Sagara.

sanskrit: apatyalābhaḥ sumahān bhaviṣyati tavānagha kīrtiṃ cāpratimāṃ loke prāpsyase puruṣarṣabha
english: O sinless one, you shall obtain an exceedingly great progeny, and you shall win incomparable fame in the world, O bull among men.

sanskrit: ekā janayitā tāta putraṃ vaṃśakaraṃ tava ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi aparā janayiṣyati
english: One wife, dear son, shall bear a single son to continue your lineage; the other shall bring forth sixty thousand sons.

sanskrit: bhāṣamāṇaṃ naravyāghraṃ rājapatnyau prasādya tam ūcatuḥ paramaprīte kṛtāñjalipuṭe tadā
english: As that tiger among men was speaking, the two royal wives, greatly pleased, propitiated him and then spoke with palms folded in reverence.

sanskrit: ekaḥ kasyāḥ suto brahman kā bahūñ janayiṣyati śrotum icchāvahe brahman satyam astu vacas tava
english: O Brahmana, whose wife shall bear the single son, and which one shall give birth to many? We wish to hear this, O Brahmana -- may your words be true.

sanskrit: tayos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhṛguḥ parama dhārmikaḥ uvāca paramāṃ vāṇīṃ svacchando 'tra vidhīyatām
english: Hearing those words of the two, Bhṛgu, most righteous, spoke the highest pronouncement: Let the choice here be freely made by each of you.

sanskrit: eko vaṃśakaro vāstu bahavo vā mahābalāḥ kīrtimanto mahotsāhāḥ kā vā kaṃ varam icchati
english: Shall there be one perpetuator of the lineage, or many of great strength, famed and of mighty enterprise? Which of you desires which boon?

sanskrit: munes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā keśinī raghunandana putraṃ vaṃśakaraṃ rāma jagrāha nṛpasaṃnidhau
english: O delight of the Raghus, O Rāma, having heard the sage's words, Keśinī, in the king's presence, chose the single son who would continue the lineage.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi suparṇabhaginī tadā mahotsāhān kīrtimato jagrāha sumatiḥ sutān
english: Then Sumatī, sister of Suparṇa, chose the sixty thousand sons, mighty in enterprise and famed.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam ṛṣiṃ kṛtvā śirasābhipraṇamya ca jagāma svapuraṃ rājā sabhāryā raghunandana
english: O delight of the Raghus, circumambulating the sage and bowing the head in reverence, the king departed to his own city together with his wives.

sanskrit: atha kāle gate tasmiñ jyeṣṭhā putraṃ vyajāyata asamañja iti khyātaṃ keśinī sagarātmajam
english: Then, when that time had come, the elder wife gave birth to a son -- Keśinī bore the son of Sagara who became known as Asamañja.

sanskrit: sumatis tu naravyāghra garbhatumbaṃ vyajāyata ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi tumbabhedād viniḥsṛtāḥ
english: But Sumatī, O tiger among men, gave birth to a gourd-womb; and from the bursting of that gourd emerged sixty thousand sons.

sanskrit: ghṛtapūrṇeṣu kumbheṣu dhātryas tān samavardhayan kālena mahatā sarve yauvanaṃ pratipedire
english: Nursemaids nurtured them in pots filled with clarified butter; after a great span of time they all attained youth.

sanskrit: atha dīrgheṇa kālena rūpayauvanaśālinaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi sagarasyābhavaṃs tadā
english: Then, after a long time had passed, the sixty thousand sons of Sagara were endowed with beauty and the vigour of youth.

sanskrit: sa ca jyeṣṭho naraśreṣṭha sagarasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ bālān gṛhītvā tu jale sarayvā raghunandana prakṣipya prahasan nityaṃ majjatas tān nirīkṣya vai
english: And that eldest, O best of men, O delight of the Raghus, the son born of Sagara's own body -- he would seize children, hurl them laughing into the waters of the Sarayū, and watch them as they sank.

sanskrit: paurāṇām ahite yuktaḥ pitrā nirvāsitaḥ purāt
english: Engaged in the harm of the townspeople, he was banished from the city by his own father.

sanskrit: tasya putro 'ṃśumān nāma asamañjasya vīryavān saṃmataḥ sarvalokasya sarvasyāpi priyaṃvadaḥ
english: Asamañja's son was named Aṃśumān, a man of valour, esteemed by all the world, pleasing in speech to all.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālena mahatā matiḥ samabhijāyata sagarasya naraśreṣṭha yajeyam iti niścitā
english: Then, after a great span of time, there arose in the mind of Sagara, O best of men, the firm resolve: I shall perform the great sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā niścayaṃ rājā sopādhyāyagaṇas tadā yajñakarmaṇi vedajño yaṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Having made that resolve, the king, together with his company of preceptors, learned in the Vedas in the matter of the sacrifice, began to prepare to perform the rite.

sanskrit: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā kathānte raghunandana uvāca paramaprīto muniṃ dīptam ivānalam
english: O delight of the Raghus, hearing Viśvāmitra's words at the tale's end, Rāma, exceedingly delighted, spoke to the sage who blazed like a fire.

sanskrit: śrotum ichāmi bhadraṃ te vistareṇa kathām imām pūrvako me kathaṃ brahman yajñaṃ vai samupāharat
english: I wish to hear this tale in full detail -- may it be well with you, O Brahmana. How did my ancestor perform that sacrifice?

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu kākutstham uvāca prahasann iva śrūyatāṃ vistaro rāma sagarasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra, smiling, then said to Kākutstha: O Rāma, let the full account of that great-souled Sagara be heard.

sanskrit: śaṃkaraśvaśuro nāma himavān acalottamaḥ vindhyaparvatam āsādya nirīkṣete parasparam
english: The Himavān, the supreme among mountains, father-in-law of Śaṃkara, and the Vindhya mountain face each other in mutual regard.

sanskrit: tayor madhye pravṛtto 'bhūd yajñaḥ sa puruṣottama sa hi deśo naravyāghra praśasto yajñakarmaṇi
english: Between those two the sacrifice was commenced, O best of men. For that region, O tiger among men, is celebrated for the performance of sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: tasyāśvacaryāṃ kākutstha dṛḍhadhanvā mahārathaḥ aṃśumān akarot tāta sagarasya mate sthitaḥ
english: O Kākutstha, dear son, Aṃśumān, firm of bow and great chariot-warrior, guarded the sacrificial horse, abiding by Sagara's command.

sanskrit: tasya parvaṇi taṃ yajñaṃ yajamānasya vāsavaḥ rākṣasīṃ tanum āsthāya yajñiyāśvam apāharat
english: During that sacrifice's sacred juncture, Vāsava -- taking on a rākṣasa form -- stole away the sacrificial horse from the one performing the rite.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇe tu kākutstha tasminn aśve mahātmanaḥ upādhyāya gaṇāḥ sarve yajamānam athābruvan
english: O Kākutstha, when that horse of the great-souled one was being carried away, all the companies of preceptors then addressed the sacrificer.

sanskrit: ayaṃ parvaṇi vegena yajñiyāśvo 'panīyate hartāraṃ jahi kākutstha hayaś caivopanīyatām
english: The sacrificial horse is being swiftly taken away at this sacred juncture -- O Kākutstha, slay the thief and bring the horse back.

sanskrit: yajñac chidraṃ bhavaty etat sarveṣām aśivāya naḥ tat tathā kriyatāṃ rājan yathāchidraḥ kratur bhavet
english: This breach in the sacrifice is inauspicious for all of us; therefore, O king, let it be remedied such that the rite may proceed without defect.

sanskrit: upādhyāya vacaḥ śrutvā tasmin sadasi pārthivaḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Hearing the preceptors' words in that assembly, the king then spoke these words to his sixty thousand sons.

sanskrit: gatiṃ putrā na paśyāmi rakṣasāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ mantrapūtair mahābhāgair āsthito hi mahākratuḥ
english: O sons, O bulls among men, I see no passage for rākṣasas here, for this great rite is guarded by the greatly blessed ones who are purified by mantras.

sanskrit: tad gacchata vicinvadhvaṃ putrakā bhadram astu vaḥ samudramālinīṃ sarvāṃ pṛthivīm anugacchata
english: Therefore go and search, O dear sons -- may it be well with you. Traverse the entire earth garlanded by the ocean.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ yojanaṃ putrā vistāram abhigacchata
english: O sons, each of you traverse one yojana in extent.

sanskrit: yāvat turagasaṃdarśas tāvat khanata medinīm tam eva hayahartāraṃ mārgamāṇā mamājñayā
english: Dig up the earth as far as you see the horse, searching for the very one who stole the horse, by my command.

sanskrit: dīkṣitaḥ pautrasahitaḥ sopādhyāyagaṇo hy aham iha sthāsyāmi bhadraṃ vo yāvat turagadarśanam
english: For I, having taken the sacrificial initiation, along with my grandson and the company of preceptors, shall remain here -- may it be well with you -- until the horse is found.

sanskrit: ity uktvā hṛṣṭamanaso rājaputrā mahābalāḥ jagmur mahītalaṃ rāma pitur vacanayantritāḥ
english: O Rāma, having heard these words, the mighty princes went forth with joyful hearts upon the surface of the earth, governed by their father's command.

sanskrit: yojanāyām avistāram ekaiko dharaṇītalam bibhiduḥ puruṣavyāghra vajrasparśasamair bhujaiḥ
english: O tiger among men, each one dug through the surface of the earth to a depth and breadth of one yojana with arms whose touch was like the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śūlair aśanikalpaiś ca halaiś cāpi sudāruṇaiḥ bhidyamānā vasumatī nanāda raghunandana
english: O delight of the Raghus, as the earth was being cleft by spears like unto lightning-bolts and by most terrible ploughshares, it cried out.

sanskrit: nāgānāṃ vadhyamānānām asurāṇāṃ ca rāghava rākṣasānāṃ ca durdharṣaḥ sattvānāṃ ninado 'bhavat
english: O Rāghava, there arose an uproar from creatures difficult to overpower -- from nāgas, asuras, and rākṣasas being slain.

sanskrit: yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭiṃ tu raghunandana bibhidur dharaṇīṃ vīrā rasātalam anuttamam
english: O delight of the Raghus, those heroes cleaved through the earth for sixty thousand yojanas until they reached the netherworld, Rasātala.

sanskrit: evaṃ parvatasaṃbādhaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ nṛpātmajāḥ khananto nṛpaśārdūla sarvataḥ paricakramuḥ
english: O tiger among kings, thus digging, the royal princes traversed Jambūdvīpa in all its mountain-thronged extent on every side.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ sāsurāḥ sahapannagāḥ saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve pitāmaham upāgaman
english: Then all the gods together with the gandharvas, the asuras, and the nāgas, their minds deeply troubled, came to the Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: te prasādya mahātmānaṃ viṣaṇṇavadanās tadā ūcuḥ paramasaṃtrastāḥ pitāmaham idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having propitiated the great-souled one, with downcast faces and greatly terrified, they then spoke these words to the Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: bhagavan pṛthivī sarvā khanyate sagarātmajaiḥ bahavaś ca mahātmāno vadhyante jalacāriṇaḥ
english: O Blessed One, the entire earth is being dug up by the sons of Sagara, and many great-souled beings that move in water are being slain.

sanskrit: ayaṃ yajñahano 'smākam anenāśvo 'panīyate iti te sarvabhūtāni nighnanti sagarātmajaḥ
english: Declaring 'This one has ruined our sacrifice -- this one has stolen the horse' -- the sons of Sagara are slaying all creatures.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavān vai pitāmahaḥ pratyuvāca susaṃtrastān kṛtāntabalamohitān
english: Having heard the words of the gods, the blessed Pitāmaha replied to those greatly terrified ones who were bewildered by the power of Fate.

sanskrit: yasyeyaṃ vasudhā kṛtsnā vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ kāpilaṃ rūpam āsthāya dhārayaty aniśaṃ dharām
english: This entire earth belongs to Vāsudeva the wise, who, having assumed the form of Kapila, bears her unceasingly.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāś cāpi nirbhedo dṛṣṭa eva sanātanaḥ sagarasya ca putrāṇāṃ vināśo 'dīrghajīvinām
english: The breaking asunder of the earth and likewise the destruction of the short-lived sons of Sagara -- both are indeed already seen to be the eternal decree.

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā trayas triṃśad ariṃdamaḥ devāḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭāḥ punar jagmur yathāgatam
english: Hearing the Pitāmaha's words, the thirty-three gods, the subduers of foes, were exceedingly gladdened and returned the way they had come.

sanskrit: sagarasya ca putrāṇāṃ prādur āsīn mahātmanām pṛthivyāṃ bhidyamānāyāṃ nirghātasamanisvanaḥ
english: As the earth was being cloven, there arose among the great-souled sons of Sagara a sound like the crash of a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato bhittvā mahīṃ sarvāṃ kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam sahitāḥ sagarāḥ sarve pitaraṃ vākyam abruvan
english: Then, having cleft through the entire earth and performed the circumambulation, all the sons of Sagara together spoke these words to their father.

sanskrit: parikrāntā mahī sarvā sattvavantaś ca sūditāḥ devadānavarakṣāṃsi piśācoragakiṃnarāḥ
english: The entire earth has been traversed, and beings of power have been slain -- gods, dānavas, rākṣasas, piśācas, serpents, and kiṃnaras.

sanskrit: na ca paśyāmahe 'śvaṃ tam aśvahartāram eva ca kiṃ kariṣyāma bhadraṃ te buddhir atra vicāryatām
english: Yet we see neither that horse nor the one who stole it. What shall we do? May it be well with you -- let your wisdom be deliberated upon in this matter.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā putrāṇāṃ rājasattamaḥ samanyur abravīd vākyaṃ sagaro raghunandana
english: O delight of the Raghus, hearing those words of his sons, Sagara, the best of kings, spoke with anger.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ khanata bhadraṃ vo nirbhidya vasudhātalam aśvahartāram āsādya kṛtārthāś ca nivartatha
english: Dig further -- may it be well with you -- cleaving through the floor of the earth; having found the thief of the horse, return having accomplished your purpose.

sanskrit: pitur vacanam āsthāya sagarasya mahātmanaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi rasātalam abhidravan
english: Abiding by the command of their father, the great-souled Sagara, the sixty thousand sons rushed down into Rasātala.

sanskrit: khanyamāne tatas tasmin dadṛśuḥ parvatopamam diśāgajaṃ virūpākṣaṃ dhārayantaṃ mahītalam
english: As the digging continued there, they then beheld Virūpākṣa, the directional elephant, mountain-like, bearing up the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: saparvatavanāṃ kṛtsnāṃ pṛthivīṃ raghunandana śirasā dhārayām āsa virūpākṣo mahāgajaḥ
english: O delight of the Raghus, that great elephant Virūpākṣa bore upon his head the entire earth with all its mountains and forests.

sanskrit: yadā parvaṇi kākutstha viśramārthaṃ mahāgajaḥ khedāc cālayate śīrṣaṃ bhūmikampas tadhā bhavet
english: O Kākutstha, whenever at a sacred juncture that great elephant, wearied, shakes his head for the sake of rest, an earthquake then occurs.

sanskrit: taṃ te pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā diśāpālaṃ mahāgajam mānayanto hi te rāma jagmur bhittvā rasātalam
english: O Rāma, circumambulating him and honouring that great elephant, guardian of the direction, they went onward cleaving through Rasātala.

sanskrit: tataḥ pūrvāṃ diśaṃ bhittvā dakṣiṇāṃ bibhiduḥ punaḥ dakṣiṇasyām api diśi dadṛśus te mahāgajam
english: Then, having cleft through the eastern direction, they again cleft through the southern; in the southern direction too they beheld a great elephant.

sanskrit: mahāpadmaṃ mahātmānaṃ sumahāparvatopamam śirasā dhārayantaṃ te vismayaṃ jagmur uttamam
english: They gazed with the utmost wonder at Mahāpadma, the great-souled one, like unto a very great mountain, bearing the earth upon his head.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā sagarasya mahātmanaḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi paścimāṃ bibhidur diśam
english: Then, having made the circumambulation, the sixty thousand sons of the great-souled Sagara cleft through the western direction.

sanskrit: paścimāyām api diśi mahāntam acalopamam diśāgajaṃ saumanasaṃ dadṛśus te mahābalāḥ
english: In the western direction too those mighty ones beheld a great directional elephant named Saumanasa, like unto a great immovable mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ te pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā pṛṣṭvā cāpi nirāmayam khanantaḥ samupakrāntā diśaṃ somavatīṃ tadā
english: Circumambulating him and also enquiring after his well-being, they then, continuing to dig, advanced towards the direction of Somavatī.

sanskrit: uttarasyāṃ raghuśreṣṭha dadṛśur himapāṇḍuram bhadraṃ bhadreṇa vapuṣā dhārayantaṃ mahīm imām
english: In the northern direction, O best of the Raghus, they beheld Bhadra -- white as snow, bearing this earth with an auspicious form.

sanskrit: samālabhya tataḥ sarve kṛtvā cainaṃ pradakṣiṇam ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇi bibhidur vasudhātalam
english: Then touching him and circumambulating him, all sixty thousand sons cleaved through the floor of the earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāguttarāṃ gatvā sāgarāḥ prathitāṃ diśam roṣād abhyakhanan sarve pṛthivīṃ sagarātmajāḥ
english: Then, going to the renowned north-eastern direction, all the sons of Sagara, in fury dug through the earth.

sanskrit: dadṛśuḥ kapilaṃ tatra vāsudevaṃ sanātanam hayaṃ ca tasya devasya carantam avidūrataḥ
english: There they beheld Kapila, the eternal Vāsudeva, and the horse of that divine one wandering not far away.

sanskrit: te taṃ yajñahanaṃ jñātvā krodhaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ abhyadhāvanta saṃkruddhās tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābruvan
english: Knowing him to be the destroyer of their sacrifice, with eyes distraught with rage, they rushed upon him in fury, crying out: Stand, stand!

sanskrit: asmākaṃ tvaṃ hi turagaṃ yajñiyaṃ hṛtavān asi durmedhas tvaṃ hi saṃprāptān viddhi naḥ sagarātmajān
english: You it is who has stolen our sacrificial horse, O dull-witted one! Know that we, the sons of Sagara, have arrived to reckon with you.

sanskrit: śrutvā tad vacanaṃ teṣāṃ kapilo raghunandana roṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭo huṃkāram akarot tadā
english: O delight of the Raghus, hearing those words of theirs, Kapila, seized by great wrath, then uttered the syllable hum.

sanskrit: tatas tenāprameyena kapilena mahātmanā bhasmarāśīkṛtāḥ sarve kākutstha sagarātmajāḥ
english: Then by that immeasurable great-souled Kapila, O Kākutstha, all the sons of Sagara were reduced to heaps of ash.
